description: The two controls a generated interface most reliably leaves half-done. A field inherits enough browser chrome to pass a glance, and a dropdown is invisible until someone opens it, so nobody opens it. Written against references/code/fields-and-dropdowns.md.

gates.title: Fields Sit On Their Own Surface
gates.rule: The field background is a token distinct from the page ground behind it, in all three themes. A field the same colour as the page is a label with a border, and readers stop seeing it as somewhere to type.
gates.fix: Define a field surface token per theme and apply it to input, textarea, and select.

gates.title: Field Borders Clear 3:1
gates.rule: The border is a UI boundary, so it needs 3:1 against the surface behind it in every theme. A hairline that only just shows in light mode is gone in gray.
gates.fix: Raise the border token's contrast, or carry the boundary with a surface shift instead.

gates.title: Placeholder Is Not The Label
gates.rule: A placeholder disappears the moment there is content, taking the field's meaning with it. Every field keeps a visible label, and the placeholder clears 4.5:1 rather than sitting at the pale grey that comes for free.
gates.fix: Add the visible label, and lift the placeholder colour onto a token that clears 4.5:1.

gates.title: One Control Height, Shared
gates.rule: Input, select, and button take the same height token, with a 44px floor on touch. A 38px input beside a 44px button is the most common tuning miss in a generated form.
gates.fix: Define a control height token and reference it from every control rule.

gates.title: Field Text Is At Least 16px
gates.rule: Below 16px, iOS zooms the whole page when the field takes focus and leaves the reader zoomed in. This holds even where the surrounding type is smaller.
gates.fix: Set font-size: max(16px, <your token>) on the field.

gates.title: Invalid Is Not Colour Alone
gates.rule: An invalid field carries aria-invalid, a message, and an icon or marker. A red border says nothing to a screen reader and little to a colourblind reader.
gates.fix: Set aria-invalid on the field and pair the colour with a message and a marker.

gates.title: Native Select Chrome Is Replaced Or Kept On Purpose
gates.rule: A bare select renders OS chrome that ignores every token. Either style the native control with appearance: none and your own chevron, keeping the platform's option list and its accessibility, or build a real listbox. State which route was taken.
gates.fix: Set appearance: none on the select and supply the chevron, padding for it, and the field surface.

gates.title: A Custom Listbox Owes The Whole Contract
gates.rule: Replacing the native select means rebuilding all of it: arrow keys cycling and wrapping, Home and End, Enter or Space to select, Escape to close without selecting, typeahead, aria-expanded mirroring visibility, role listbox or menu, aria-selected on options, focus returning to the trigger on close, and outside-click dismissal. A div with a click handler is not a select.
gates.fix: Use the platform Popover API or a headless primitive rather than hand-rolling the contract.

gates.title: Menu Is Not Clipped By An Ancestor
gates.rule: A menu inside an overflow-hidden or overflow-auto ancestor is cut off at the container edge, and it looks like a rendering bug rather than a layout one. Portal it to the body or use the Popover API, which handles stacking and light-dismiss on its own.
gates.fix: Portal the menu, or move to the Popover API.

gates.title: Menu Flips At The Viewport Edge
gates.rule: A menu near the bottom of the viewport opens upward; near the right edge it aligns right. Without it the last option is unreachable on a laptop and the menu runs off the screen on a phone.
gates.fix: Use a positioning library or the Popover API's anchor handling rather than a fixed offset.

gates.title: Menu Has A Max Height And Scrolls Inside Itself
gates.rule: A menu is capped at something like min(320px, 60vh) with overflow-y auto and overscroll-behavior contain, so a long list never exceeds the viewport and scrolling it never scrolls the page behind.
gates.fix: Add the max-height, overflow-y: auto, and overscroll-behavior: contain to the menu surface.

gates.title: Menu Surface Is Opaque And Elevated
gates.rule: The menu has its own raised surface token, a border or shadow separating it from what it covers, and no transparency. A translucent menu over body text is unreadable and reads as unfinished.
gates.fix: Give the menu a raised surface token, a rule, and a shadow, and drop any alpha from its background.

gates.title: Menu Sits On The Named Z-Layer
gates.rule: The menu takes its stacking from the layer scale, above the page and below modals. A z-index of 9999 is a guess that collides with the next guess.
gates.fix: Add a dropdown step to the z-index scale and reference it.

gates.title: Menu Does Not Push Page Content
gates.rule: The menu is absolutely or fixed positioned. A menu in normal flow shoves everything below it down as it opens, which reads as the page breaking.
gates.fix: Position the menu absolutely against a positioned parent, or portal it.

gates.title: Menu Width Relates To Its Trigger
gates.rule: The menu is at least the trigger's width and does not jump between openings as its content changes. A menu narrower than the control it belongs to reads as detached from it.
gates.fix: Set min-width to the trigger's width, measured or via the anchor's size.

gates.title: Hover, Focused, And Selected Are Three Distinct States
gates.rule: Arrowing through a menu while the mouse rests on a different row must not light two rows the same way. Hover is a surface tint; focused adds a marker such as a left rule or ring; selected is the current value.
gates.fix: Give the focused option a marker the hover state does not have.

gates.title: Selected Carries A Marker In A Reserved Gutter
gates.rule: The current value is marked by a check or dot, not by colour alone, and the gutter holding it is reserved on every row so labels do not shift when the selection moves.
gates.fix: Reserve the marker column on all options and render the marker only on the selected one.

gates.title: Long Option Labels Stay Readable
gates.rule: A label longer than the menu truncates with the full text reachable through a title, a tooltip, or a two-line wrap. A label sliced mid-word with no way to read it is a dead end.
gates.fix: Truncate with an ellipsis and expose the full string.

gates.title: Menu Has Empty And Loading States
gates.rule: A filtered menu with no matches says so, and one that fetches its options shows placeholder rows. An empty box reads as broken.
gates.fix: Add the no-results row and, where options are fetched, placeholder rows in the option's shape.

gates.title: Menu Opens From Its Trigger, Fast
gates.rule: 150 to 250ms, ease-out, scaling from the trigger's transform-origin rather than its own centre, and stopped under reduced motion.
gates.fix: Set the popover transform-origin variable and cap the duration.

gates.title: Date, Time, And Colour Pickers Follow The Same Rules
gates.rule: The trigger is a field, the panel is a menu, and the grid inside needs six states, not three: hover, focused, selected, today, out-of-range, and disabled. The native picker indicator is themed too, or it renders as the platform's icon on the wrong background.
gates.fix: Theme the calendar picker indicator per theme and give the grid all six states.

gates.title: Checkbox, Radio, And Switch Are Themed
gates.rule: accent-color set from the accent token gets these right cheaply on modern browsers. A custom one still owes the focus ring, the 44px hit area, and the native semantics — a switch is a checkbox whatever it looks like.
gates.fix: Set accent-color on the inputs, or give the custom control its focus ring and semantics.

gates.title: Autofilled Fields Keep The Design's Colours
gates.rule: A browser paints its own pale yellow over a field it filled and keeps it through hover and focus, and background-color does not reach it. The override covers every field on the page, not only the ones the project draws: a hosted sign-in widget renders its own inputs, and those are the fields a visitor is most likely to have saved credentials for.
gates.fix: Add an unlayered :-webkit-autofill rule on input, textarea and select. Repaint the project's own fields with an inset box-shadow the height of the field, and neutralise the rest by delaying the background-color transition, which leaves each field the background it already had.
